If there are any suggestions I would highly appreciate, thank you ;-;

I'm sorry that I don't know technical terms enough to explain exactly what the issue was, but I genuinely appreciate the commenters who tried to help regardless and tried to figure out the issue with me.
We were going for tilesets B-E because A1-5 are a pain in the ass we don't want to mess with yet. I don't know what tutorials my sisters were following, but regardless everything that everyone explained really helped me better understand tilesets even if it *wasn't* the issue at hand, and I really genuinely appreciate it for things we'll need to know in the future as well.
The issue was we weren't using the correct 768x768 pixels for the canvas size, which was messing everything up. I don't know if my sister used the 48x48 grid on procreate but if they didn't, I explained to them how to do it, and when I tested it myself on my pc, it worked. So I believe it should work for them too. Our game is located on their PC, so they'll have to try it on our actual game when they wake up.
I was distracted and confused by all of the text on the Asset Standards for A1-5 that I completely missed the little bit of text at the bottom for B-E, which is why I wasn't understanding, and that's totally on me.
Thank you everyone for helping and being patient with me when I barely know what I'm talking about. You guys are great <3

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: You really haven't given enough information to make the problem clear. That said, it does sound like maybe you're putting your tiles in the wrong slot in the database. You should read the Asset Standards section of the help (accessible from the menu, or by pressing F1) – it explains in some detail how the tilesheets work and what sizes they have to be. In particular, the tiles on A1, A2, A3, and A4 are cut up into 24x24 pieces, rather than 48x48 pieces. So, it seems possible that this could explain why your flower got cut in two.

posts.author: Apocalypticat
posts.body:
Maybe this is redundant, but, to echo what Solar Flare and Dev With Coffee said - there are tutorials for this, and if you follow them, you wouldn't have this issue. Sorry to say.
To make it as simple as possible:
In your image editing program (Paint.Net, Gimp etc) let it draw you a grid that matches your game tile size. Standard MV is 48 x 48. So, let it draw you a grid of 48 x 48. Now you have your positioning grid.
Next, on a separate layer, position your created images according to this grid. If you want something to be 1 tile, keep it exactly within the bounds of 1 grid cell. A1 tilesets are different than, say B, C, D etc.
Remove the grid layer and save in applicable area, then load into your instance of RPG Maker.
This is also in many various tutorials...so again, if your images are cut off etc, then you're not actually following the tutorials.
As an example, here is a screenshot of the standard Outside B Tileset with the 48 x 48 grid applied.
